title: The pronoun y
goal: By the end of this lesson you can use y to replace a place or 'à + thing', place it correctly in all the tenses you know, and use everyday expressions like on y va, vas-y and ça y est.

body: *Y* means 'there'. It replaces a place introduced by *à, en, dans, chez, sur, sous, devant…*: *Je vais* **à Québec** → *J'***y** *vais*. *Il est* **chez lui** → *Il* **y** *est*.
English often leaves 'there' out, but French needs *y*: *Tu vas au dépanneur? Oui, j'y vais.* You cannot just say *Oui, je vais*.

head: Full sentence
With y
rows: Les clés sont dans le tiroir.

learn.tip: Tu vas où? I'm going THERE = j'y vais. Never leave the sentence hanging.

learn.h: Y replaces 'à + a thing or idea'
body: With verbs built with *à*, *y* replaces a thing, an idea or an activity: *Je pense* **à mon voyage** → *J'***y** *pense*. *Tu joues* **au hockey**? *Oui, j'***y** *joue*.
For a **person** after *à*, use *lui / leur* (lesson 45) or *à lui / à elle* with *penser*: *Je pense* **à ma mère** → *Je pense* **à elle** (not *j'y pense*).

Same place as the other object pronouns: before the conjugated verb (*j'y vais*), before the infinitive (*je vais y aller*), before *avoir / être* in the passé composé (*j'y suis allé*), and *ne…pas* around them (*je n'y vais pas*, *je n'y suis jamais allé*).
With two pronouns, *y* comes after the others: *Je* **t'y** *emmène* (I'll take you there). *Il* **m'y** *a invité*.

In a positive command *y* follows the verb: *Allons-***y**! *Allez-***y**! For *tu* commands of *aller* and *-er* verbs, the lost *-s* comes back before *y* for the sound: *Va* → **Vas-y**! *Pense* → **Penses-y**!

You already know *il y a*. Others are everywhere in daily life: *On y va?* (Shall we go?), *Vas-y!* (Go ahead! / Go for it!), *Ça y est!* (That's it! Done!), *J'y suis!* (I've got it!), *Je n'y peux rien* (There's nothing I can do about it).
One spelling note: with the future of *aller* (*j'irai*), French drops *y* to avoid 'y i': *J'irai* demain (not *j'y irai*).

examples.fr: Tu vas au marché Jean-Talon? Oui, j'y vais samedi.
examples.en: Are you going to the Jean-Talon Market? Yes, I'm going (there) on Saturday.

examples.fr: Mes parents habitent à Gatineau depuis 1990. Ils y habitent depuis longtemps.
examples.en: My parents have lived in Gatineau since 1990. They've lived there a long time.

examples.fr: On va y aller en métro.
examples.en: We're going to go there by metro.

examples.fr: Je suis allée en Gaspésie l'été passé. J'y ai vu des baleines.
examples.en: I went to the Gaspé Peninsula last summer. I saw whales there.

examples.fr: Tu penses à tes vacances? J'y pense tout le temps!
examples.en: Are you thinking about your vacation? I think about it all the time!

examples.fr: Tu as répondu à sa question? Non, je n'y ai pas répondu.
examples.en: Did you answer his question? No, I didn't answer it.

examples.fr: Il joue au hockey depuis l'âge de cinq ans. Il y joue tous les jours.
examples.en: He's played hockey since he was five. He plays it every day.
Winter? I'm slowly getting used to it.

examples.fr: Tu crois aux fantômes? Non, je n'y crois pas.
examples.en: Do you believe in ghosts? No, I don't believe in them.
You want to try? Go ahead!
examples.note: the -s of va comes back before y

examples.fr: Ça y est, j'ai fini mon rapport!
examples.en: That's it, I've finished my report!
examples.note: ça y est = done / here we go

examples.en: Your appointment, think about it! (don't forget!)

examples.fr: Je pense souvent à ma grand-mère. Je pense souvent à elle.
examples.en: I often think about my grandmother. I often think about her.
examples.note: a person after penser à: à elle, not y

examples.fr: Il m'y a emmené en voiture.

quebec.intro: Quebecers use y even more than the textbook. 'Je vais' is very often 'j'vas', so 'j'y vais' becomes 'j'y vas'. You will also hear 'vas-y', 'envoye' and 'on y va-tu?' constantly.

items.note: envoye / envoyez = go on, hurry; informal (lesson 31)

drills.why: A place after à = y, before the verb.
With penser à + person, use à lui / à elle, not y.
The -s returns before y, with a hyphen.

options: Je ne suis pas y allé.

drills.q: Le cinéma? On ___ va ce soir. (there)

drills.en: Your exam? Are you thinking about it?

drills.q: Montréal? Nous allons ___ habiter l'an prochain. (there)
drills.en: Montreal? We're going to live there next year.
We're going to go there tomorrow.

drills.why: Two common ways to say let's go.

vocab.en: that's it, done, here we go

vocab.ex: Les clés sont dans le tiroir.
On a vu des baleines à Tadoussac.
J'ai un rendez-vous chez le dentiste.

pron.tip: [ji vè], two syllables: y is just an [i] sound.
juh-ni-swi-ja-mè-a-LÉ; casual: j'y suis jamais allé.

listen.title: Une fin de semaine à Québec

dialogue.fr: Non, je n'y suis jamais allée. Toi?
Oui, j'y vais chaque hiver pour le Carnaval.
dialogue.en: Yes, I go every winter for the Carnival.

dialogue.fr: Oui, mais on s'y habitue. Veux-tu venir avec moi cette année?
dialogue.en: Yes, but you get used to it. Do you want to come with me this year?

dialogue.fr: Penses-y vite, il reste juste quelques chambres à l'hôtel!
dialogue.en: Think about it quickly, there are only a few hotel rooms left!

dialogue.fr: OK, ça y est, j'ai décidé: on y va!
dialogue.en: OK, that's it, I've decided: let's go!

questions.q: Has B been to Quebec City?
When does A go to Quebec City?

speak.prompt: Answer with y: 'Tu vas souvent au cinéma? Tu es déjà allé(e) à Tadoussac? Tu penses à tes vacances?'
speak.model: Oui, j'y vais une fois par mois. Non, je n'y suis jamais allé. Oui, j'y pense tout le temps!

speak.prompt: Encourage a friend who is nervous before a hockey game, using vas-y, allez and ça y est.
speak.model: Vas-y, t'es capable! Allez, on y va! … Ça y est, tu as marqué!

speak.prompt: Say 'I'm going there now' the standard way and the casual Quebec way.
speak.model: J'y vais maintenant. / J'y vas, là.

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about a place you go regularly (gym, café, cottage…). Name the place once, then use y in at least four sentences, including one in the passé composé and one with the futur proche.
write.model: Le samedi matin, je vais au marché Jean-Talon. J'y vais à pied parce que j'habite tout près. J'y achète des fruits et du fromage. La semaine passée, j'y ai rencontré une ancienne collègue. On va y retourner ensemble samedi prochain. J'y pense déjà!

quiz.q: 'Tu réponds à la lettre?' — 'Oui, j'___ réponds.'
Where does y go? 'Je veux ___ aller ___.'
quiz.why: Before the infinitive it belongs to: je veux y aller.

quiz.q: What does 'J'y vas' mean in Quebec speech?
quiz.why: J'vas = je vais, so j'y vas = j'y vais.
Ça y est signals something is done or has just happened.

quiz.q: Which is the standard future of 'I'll go there'?
quiz.why: Y is dropped before forms of aller starting with i: j'irai.
